note.note:
Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure:
  - Generalized body aches and fatigue for at least six weeks.
  - Noted transient skin rash on posterior calf, first observed mid to late February; no clear trigger, no recognized tick or insect bite reported despite outdoor activity and travel.
- Symptom timeline and progression:
  - Last felt well around Christmas/New Year.
  - Symptoms began a couple of weeks after returning from holiday in the United States (late January/early February).
  - Rash appeared mid to late February, resolved after a couple of weeks.
  - Ongoing reduced energy, tiredness, generalized aches.
- ENT symptoms:
  - No persistent sore throat (noted only mild sore throat at time of rash, possibly with low-grade fever).
  - No difficulty swallowing, no odynophagia, no drooling, no voice changes, no nasal/ocular symptoms, no stridor/noisy breathing, no dyspnea.
  - No facial, lip, tongue, or uvular swelling reported.
  - No ear pain/hearing loss or neck pain/swelling.
- Relevant past episodes and treatments:
  - No documented prior similar episodes.
  - No recent infections reported prior to onset.
  - No prior hospitalizations or injection therapy reported.
- Allergies and current medications:
  - Allergic rhinitis/hay fever and asthma.
  - Asthma controlled; uses a preventative inhaler (dose/route/frequency not documented, stated to use morning and night).
  - Regular antihistamine use (name, dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - No explicit drug or food allergy list provided.
- Relevant social context:
  - Lives with wife; works for a health technology company.
  - Has been able to continue working but notes reduced effectiveness.

Objective:
- Observable swelling and distribution:
  - Rash: described as non-itchy, posterior calf, resolved over ~2 weeks; photo shown during consult.
  - No active rashes, no joint swelling.
- Airway/breathing:
  - No airway or breathing difficulties reported or observed.
- Mental status/associated features:
  - No dizziness, syncope, headache or visual changes except for mild general “crappy” feeling.
  - Cognitively intact.
- Vitals and examination findings:
  - Not recorded.
- Presence of another person:
  - Lives with wife; no details on accompaniment during consult.

Assessment:
- Suspected post-infectious or inflammatory syndrome with fatigue and past rash; differential includes possible Lyme disease due to travel and rash history, as well as other systemic or infectious etiologies.
- Key points: subacute onset after travel, prior rash with questionable exposure, ongoing generalized fatigue and myalgias, no acute oropharyngeal/airway involvement.

Plan:
- Advised blood tests including routine panel and specific Lyme serology.
- Discussed possible diagnosis of Lyme disease and need for further evaluation pending results.
- No evidence of acute ENT airway emergency; no need for urgent intervention.
- Advised to arrange bloodwork via support line and follow-up (teleconsultation) approximately one week after results available.
- No specific medication adjustments advised at this time.
- Provided reassurance and answered patient queries.
- No specific instructions on emergency contact or red flags documented.
- No discussion of COVID-19 vaccination.
